extracted.intended_audience: Research authors preparing and submitting Registered Reports to PCI Registered Reports (PCI RR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors preparing Stage 1 and Stage 2 Registered Reports for submission to the PCI Registered Reports platform, covering evaluation criteria, workflow, procedural requirements, and expectations for transparency and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1A. The scientific validity of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: This criterion addresses the extent to which the research question is scientifically justifiable. Valid scientific questions usually stem from theory or mathematics, an intended or possible application, or an existing evidence base, and should be defined with sufficient precision as to be answerable through quantitative or qualitative research. They should also fall within established ethical norms. Note that subjective judgments about the importance, novelty or timeliness of a research question are NOT a relevant criterion at PCI RR and do not form part of this assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research questions must be precisely defined and answerable; must stem from theory, application, or evidence base; must meet ethical norms. Importance/novelty/timeliness are explicitly NOT assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1B. The logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: This criterion addresses the coherence and credibility of any a priori hypotheses. The inclusion of hypotheses is not required– a Stage 1 RR can instead propose estimation or measurement of phenomena without expecting a specific observation or relationship between variables. However, where hypotheses are stated, they should be stated as precisely as possible and follow directly from the research question or theory. A Stage 1 RR should also propose a hypothesis that is sufficiently conceivable as to be worthy of investigation. The complete evaluation of any preliminary research (and data) in the Stage 1 submission is included within this criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses (if present) must be precise and theory-linked; hypotheses are optional (estimation/measurement studies allowed). Preliminary data evaluation forms part of this assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1C. The soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: This criterion assesses the validity of the study procedures and analyses, including the presence of critical design features (e.g., internal and external validity, blinding, randomisation, rules for data inclusion and exclusion, suitability of any included pilot data) and the appropriateness of the analysis plan. For designs involving inferential statistics and hypothesis-testing, this criterion includes the rigour of the proposed sampling plan, such as a statistical power analysis or Bayesian alternative, and, where applicable, the rationale for defining any statistical priors or the smallest effect size of interest. For programmatic RRs, this criterion captures whether the separate study components justify separate Stage 2 outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include critical design features, explicit data inclusion/exclusion rules, justification of sampling plan (power or Bayesian alternatives), rationale for priors or smallest-effect-size-of-interest. Programmatic RRs require assessment of the robustness of components. Submissions judged to lack sufficient rigour here risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1D. Clarity and degree of methodological detail sufficient for close replication
rubrics_metrics.description: This criterion assesses the extent to which the Stage 1 protocol contains sufficient detail to be reproducible and ensure protection against research bias, such as analytic overfitting or vague study procedures. In general, meeting this requirement will require the method section(s) of a Stage 1 protocol to be significantly longer and more detailed than in a regular manuscript, while also being clearly structured and accessible to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors encouraged to include a design summary table linking questions, hypotheses, sampling plans, analyses, and contingent interpretation. Blinded-analyst approaches are acceptable if specified in reproducible detail and blinding is robust. Methods should be sufficiently detailed to prevent undisclosed flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1E. Consideration of sufficient outcome-neutral checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors have considered sufficient outcome-neutral conditions (e.g., absence of floor or ceiling effects; positive controls; other quality checks) for ensuring that the obtained results are able to test the stated hypotheses or answer the stated research question(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-neutral tests must be pre-specified and independent of main hypotheses (e.g., manipulation checks, parallel measurements). Examples: positive controls (Galileo example). Not always possible in all designs; where possible, must be pre-specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2A. Data ability to meet approved outcome-neutral criteria at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the data are able to test the authors’ proposed hypotheses (or answer the proposed research question) by passing the approved outcome-neutral criteria, such as absence of floor and ceiling effects or success of positive controls or other quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pre-specified outcome-neutral tests fail in critical ways, Stage 2 rejection is possible. Not all protocols can pre-specify such tests; assessment is relevant when they were specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2B. Consistency of introduction, rationale and hypotheses with Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses (where applicable) are the same as the approved Stage 1 submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aside from tense changes, typo/factual corrections, the introduction, rationale and hypotheses must remain identical. Authors must submit tracked-changes version at Stage 2 to make any changes clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2C. Adherence to registered study procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors adhered precisely to the registered study procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations after IPA must be consulted with recommender before completion of data collection; minor changes may be permitted at recommender discretion and reported in Stage 2. Substantial changes require withdrawal/resubmission as new Stage 1. All preregistered analyses must be reported except rare collectively-agreed flawed analyses (still mentioned in Methods with justification if omitted from Results). Failure to adhere may lead to Stage 2 rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2D. Justification and soundness of any unregistered exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, whether any unregistered exploratory analyses are justified, methodologically sound, and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unregistered analyses are admissible but must be clearly labeled (e.g., “Exploratory Analyses”), justified, caveated, and should not be the sole basis for conclusions. Reviewers may suggest additional tests but authors are not obliged unless necessary to meet Stage 2 criteria. Additional unregistered studies are not permitted at Stage 2 (use Incremental Registration instead).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2E. Whether authors’ conclusions are justified by the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors’ conclusions are justified given the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in Discussion, Abstract, and elsewhere must be warranted by the data. PCI RR decisions will never be based on perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replications and original research treated equally
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR welcomes submissions proposing original research and replication studies. All submissions are assessed according to the same criteria, and novelty or originality of the research is irrelevant, provided the research question is judged to be scientifically valid (criterion 1A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is not a criterion; replications assessed on same scientific validity, methods, and rigour metrics as original research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence thresholds and discipline-appropriate standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms and standards of evidence vary widely; PCI RR does not set a universal standard. For quantitative fields not using inferential stats, plan to obtain field-rigorous strength of evidence; for Neyman-Pearson inference include a priori power analysis; Bayesian analyses require specification of predictive distributions and goals for Bayes factors. No minimum power/Bayes threshold is set by PCI RR but falling short risks rejection under 1C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power analyses should use conservative/lowest plausible effect sizes; interim analyses require pre-specified inspection points, Type I correction, and stopping rules. Tools recommended (G*Power, ANOVAPower, PANGEA, SIMR, etc.). Authors aiming for PCI RR-friendly journals should meet journals' minimum evidential standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approval policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In fields where ethics approval is required, authors should generally ensure approvals are in place before Stage 1 submission. PCI RR may perform Stage 1 review before ethics approval in specific cases but any IPA will be provisional pending confirmation of ethics approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional IPA does not trigger automatic acceptance by PCI RR-friendly journals (they require ethics approval). Authors considering Stage 1 before ethics approval should consult Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding approval policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should generally ensure sufficient funding/resources are in place before Stage 1 submission. Exceptions: major public-importance proposals or Registered Report Funding Partnerships (RRFPs) where PCI RR may review before funding; any IPA in these cases will be provisional pending funding confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRFPs allow concurrent funder and PCI RR review. Authors considering submission before funding should consult Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRs involving existing data — Levels of bias control (Levels 1–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy defining bias-control levels for submissions using existing data: Level 6 = data do not yet exist (primary RRs); Levels 1–5 denote increasing prior access/observation of data and corresponding required countermeasures. Submissions Level 1+ are eligible; Level 0 (authors know outcomes) is ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must identify which level applies; article labelled with level on PCI RR. If parts of study are at different levels, the whole article is assigned the lowest level among components. Lower levels (1 or 2) usually require stringent countermeasures (conservative thresholds, blinded analysts, multiverse/specification analyses). Dropping bias-control level after data collection starts can increase rejection risk and reduce eligibility for some PCI RR-friendly journals. Authors cannot submit studies where they already know prospective analysis outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of preliminary and pilot studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may include preliminary/pilot studies in Stage 1 to establish questions, generate hypotheses, estimate effect sizes, or demonstrate feasibility. Preliminary studies will be published in Stage 2 and must be clearly distinguished from preregistered protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective research must stand independently of preliminary outcomes. Overreliance on preliminary results can lead to rejection under 1A, 1B, or 1C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol preregistration and embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: At Stage 1 IPA, PCI RR will preregister the approved manuscript on OSF via a dedicated Stage 1 RR preregistration mechanism. The Stage 1 manuscript will be public or under private embargo (up to 4 years) until Stage 2 submission. PCI RR preregisters the protocol only after IPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must agree that if they withdraw after IPA, PCI RR may lift embargo and publish a short summary in Withdrawn Registrations. Stage 2 abstract must include direct URL and date of preregistration. Clinical trial registration should still occur as per discipline requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of registered and unregistered analyses at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered analyses' outcomes must be reported in the manuscript except in rare jointly-agreed cases of logical flaws. Unregistered analyses may be included but must be clearly identified, justified, caveated, and not form the sole basis of conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend separate headings like “Exploratory Analyses”. Unregistered additional studies are not permitted at Stage 2 — use Incremental Registration for new studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol deviations and change management at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from approved procedures after IPA, regardless of perceived minor nature, could lead to Stage 2 rejection. Authors must consult the recommender before completing data collection if deviations occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientifically essential, low-bias-increasing changes likely to be approved and reported. Substantial changes require readmission to Stage 1 or withdrawal/resubmission. Stage 2 must include tracked changes and footnotes explaining deviations (what changed, why, when, how integrity was maintained, recommender approval). New literature after IPA belongs in Discussion not Introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials transparency (TOP compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR is a signatory of the TOP guidelines. Authors are required to make all study data, digital materials, and code publicly available at Stage 2 to the maximum extent allowed by legal/ethical restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult PCI RR TOP policy before Stage 1. Open Data/Materials/Preregistered badges are awarded per policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn registrations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors withdraw after IPA, PCI RR will publicly mark the Stage 1 recommendation as 'withdrawn' and include a statement explaining key facts and reason. Private embargoes will be lifted and protocol made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial withdrawals (publishing part of a registered plan) are generally not possible except for components of programmatic RRs planned as separate Stage 2 outputs. Authors must provide estimated Stage 2 submission dates; failure to submit within 6 months of agreed deadline and being non-responsive will be treated as withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental registration requirement for adding studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who wish to add further studies to a registered plan at Stage 2 must use Incremental Registration rather than including additional unregistered studies in the Stage 2 manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Section truncated in source) Incremental Registration allows additions planned as new Stage 1 components; unregistered additional studies at Stage 2 are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review and anonymous review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR publishes all reviews of recommended manuscripts; reviewers may sign or remain anonymous (except when an author is a Managing Board member; in that case, reviews must be signed). All Stage 1 and Stage 2 reviews and recommender decision letters are published no later than Stage 2 acceptance. Reviews of rejected submissions are not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit anonymously at Stage 1 (instructions provided). Reviewers/recommenders must adhere to PCI RR code of conduct; violating reviews may be returned for editing or discarded. Authors and reviewers should refrain from self-publishing review content during review or after rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender triage and desk decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are evaluated by recommenders before specialist peer review as part of triage. Only submissions judged to meet or nearly meet criteria are sent for specialist peer review. Submissions that fail but have potential may be desk-rejected with invitation to resubmit; those substantially short will be desk-rejected outright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommender triage aims to ensure peer review resources focus on near-ready submissions; triage feedback may include specific revision suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard review vs Scheduled review tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR offers two Stage 1 peer-review tracks: Standard review (full Stage 1 manuscript; first round ~4–8 weeks) and Scheduled review (one-page snapshot, triage, then coordinated review during a scheduled week with authors preparing full manuscript in the interim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduled review requires use of the 1-page snapshot template (PDF at repository such as OSF) and cannot use Google Drive. Scheduled review can significantly accelerate the first-round assessment but only expedites first round, not re-review. Both tracks available for Regular and Programmatic RRs. For Level 6 submissions, allow enough time between submission and planned data collection for review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of rejected manuscripts may appeal within 30 days by emailing the Managing Board or the recommender. Appeals must state why decision should change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals considered only if authors (a) identify factual errors by reviewers/recommender that had major impact, or (b) provide substantiated claim of unfair treatment/bias. Appeals meeting criteria are reviewed by a panel (recommender + two Managing Board members) and decided by majority vote; decisions following appeal are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limits and formatting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR imposes no word limits or specific formatting requirements on submissions. Manuscripts should be as concise as possible but as long as necessary for clear, comprehensive rationale and reproducible methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established disciplinary formatting conventions. Authors intending to publish in PCI RR-friendly journals should check journal-specific word/format requirements (not required for PCI RR recommendation but may be required for journal adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges for Open Practices (Open Data, Open Materials, Preregistered)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR awards Open Data, Open Materials, and Preregistered badges per its TOP guidelines policy. These badges appear alongside abstracts for recommended Stage 2 RRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCI RR TOP policy for badge criteria and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT contributor roles requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR uses the CRediT taxonomy to ensure transparent contributor acknowledgement. All Stage 2 manuscripts must include a CRediT statement (encouraged at Stage 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should list specific contributions per CRediT roles to be considered for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit and anonymous submission mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions: for anonymous Stage 1 submission, remove nominative information and post manuscript+supplementary files on a server/repository that allows anonymous sharing (OSF, GitHub, etc.), then submit the anonymous URL to PCI RR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further detailed instructions are in the 'How to...?' section; follow repository guidance for anonymous URLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising and resubmitting — response expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should respond to all reviewer and recommender comments in a point-by-point format and revise the manuscript accordingly. A track-changes version of the revised manuscript must be available to reviewers/recommender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload track-changes as a separate file or provide link. Ensure reviewers can access a version showing all textual changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased co-author policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies after Stage 1 submission, they can remain as a co-author provided changes after death would have aligned with their ideas. Authors must provide a footnote/acknowledgement stating the deceased author's contribution, stage of publication involvement, that co-authors consent to the name, and that PCI RR (and the publishing journal if applicable) were informed and agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the stated items clearly in a footnote or acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of artificial intelligence for text and code generation
rubrics_metrics.description: AI (including LLMs) can be used to translate, correct or improve text/code provided authors review and approve output. Using AI to analyse data is permitted if methods are published/cited or original and detailed. Generating text, illustrations and code using AI can be problematic due to plagiarism, hallucination and lack of human verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI cannot be listed as an author. Authors must disclose AI use in Methods or Acknowledgements when AI generated text or code is used, and carefully check for plagiarism/hallucinations/errors. Authors must not generate illustrations using AI (disallowed). Non-compliance may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal adopters categories and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Two adopter categories: PCI RR-friendly journals endorse PCI RR criteria and commit to accepting recommended manuscripts without further peer review while meeting procedural requirements (scope, word length, minimum evidential thresholds, bias-control levels). PCI RR-interested journals are alerted to IPA/Stage 2 acceptance and may contact authors or request further review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR-friendly journals will not relitigate scientific elements already approved by PCI RR; where journals set higher procedural/evidential minima, authors must meet those to gain automatic journal acceptance. Authors choosing a journal after recommendation must ensure compliance with that journal's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access, fees and charges statement
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR is free for authors and all approved Stage 2 submissions are freely available as preprints. However, PCI RR-friendly journals may charge APCs or other fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult specific journal policies for up-to-date fee information; PCI RR maintains lists indicating whether journals charge fees but authors should verify.
